title: Heat acclimatisation
text: Acclimatisation is the body's adjustment to working in heat. It takes roughly two weeks of graded exposure: the heart rate at a given effort falls, sweating starts earlier and carries less salt, and core temperature stays lower for the same work. A common schedule is about 20 percent of a normal workload on day one, adding about 20 percent each day for new workers, and a shorter ramp for workers returning after a week or more away. Acclimatisation is lost in about one to two weeks away from the heat, so it must be rebuilt after leave. Unacclimatised workers carry a much higher risk and most serious heat events happen in the first days on the job.
source: US CDC NIOSH Heat Stress, acclimatization schedules; ACGIH 2017; OSHA heat campaign
